title: Site Visit
tagline: Find the sunniest spot, and the best view, for a chill-out room.
grownUp: This mission is about where a building goes: the sun, the wind, the slope and the views. Start by pointing out the sunny meadow and the shady corner on the map together.
The Big Question has no right answer. Listen to the reasons the Architect gives, and say that architects weigh up warmth, shade and quiet in different ways.
The sun comes up in the east, so a window facing east gets the morning sun. The at-home map works best if you look at the garden at two different times of day.

steps.title: Every building starts with a site
steps.text: Every building sits on a piece of land called a site. Your map has mountains, a forest, a waterfall, a meadow, a beach and the sea.
steps.ask: Which part of the site would you like to visit first?

steps.title: Visiting the site
steps.text: Architects visit a site to look at the sun, the wind and the views. They stand where the building will go and notice what they can see.
steps.ask: What would you notice first if you stood in the meadow?

steps.title: Which way does the sun come up?
steps.prompt: Where does the sun come up in the morning?
steps.reveal: The sun comes up in the east and goes down in the west. That is why a room with a window facing east gets the morning sun.

steps.title: Build your chill-out room
steps.intro: Turn the site, move the sun, find the best view and build your chill-out room.

steps.title: Sunny meadow or cool corner?
steps.scenario: Your chill-out room could go in the sunny meadow, or in the cool misty corner by the waterfall. A third choice is under the trees at the edge of the forest.

options.label: Sunny meadow
options.detail: It is warm and bright, with a big view across the grass.

options.label: Misty corner by the waterfall
options.detail: It is cool and quiet, with the sound of the water to listen to.

options.label: Under the trees
options.detail: It is shady and sheltered, with leaves to look up at.

steps.reveal: Architects think about sun, shade, wind and quiet, and every site has a different mix of them. Some architects choose the sunny spot for warmth, and others choose the shady spot to keep cool.
steps.followUp: Where would you go to rest on a hot day, and why?

steps.title: Map the sun and the shade
need: A sunny garden or yard, with a grown-up
steps: Draw a simple map of the garden or yard, with a box for the house.
In the morning, colour in the sunny parts and the shady parts, and draw an arrow for the wind.
Go back later in the day, and colour the map again. Then compare the two maps.
steps.why: Architects check the sun, the shade and the wind at different times of day before they choose where a room goes.

debrief: Where on the site would you put a room that needs the most sun, and why?
